headline: Viral Post Claims All 'Random' Numbers Are Generated by Man Named Randy in Nebraska
subheadline: Tech companies deny existence of Randy; Nebraska tourism board embraces theory
summary: A satirical post about random number generation has convinced thousands that a man named Randy manually produces all computer randomness.
content:
What began as an obvious joke has become an unshakeable belief for a surprising number of internet users: the theory that all "random" numbers generated by computers are actually produced by a man named Randy who lives in Nebraska.

"Think about it," reads the original post by @QuantumSkeptic on Chirper. "They call it a 'random number GENERATOR.' Who's the generator? Randy. Randy is the generator. He's been doing this since 1974."

The post, which has been shared over 500,000 times, has spawned an elaborate mythology around Randy. According to believers, Randy works in a windowless facility in rural Nebraska, manually selecting numbers based on "vibes" and a complex system involving dice, coin flips, and "the energy of the corn."

"Every time your Spotify shuffles, that's Randy," explained one devoted follower. "Every lottery number? Randy. Every CAPTCHA asking you to pick random images? Those aren't random. Randy picked them. Randy always knows which ones have traffic lights."

Tech companies have issued statements denying Randy's existence, which believers interpret as confirmation. "Of course they deny it," wrote one commenter. "Randy is the most important employee they have. They can't let us know."

The Nebraska Tourism Board has taken a different approach, releasing a statement reading: "Nebraska neither confirms nor denies the existence of Randy. But if you're looking for random numbers, why not visit Nebraska? We have corn."

Dr. Elena Martinez, asked to explain how random number generation actually works, began her explanation before being interrupted. "Wait," she said, pausing. "Why is it called a generator? Who is generating?"

She has since requested time off.

Searches for "Randy Nebraska random" have increased by 847% this month.
author: Alex Rivera, Digital Culture
